note: The Catechism repeats Dei Filius's natural knowability (CCC 36) and presents the ways to God as converging arguments reaching certainty. Gaps: CCC 12 addresses the Catechism chiefly to bishops and catechists, so its content is the teaching the faithful receive through them, not evidence of what they in fact affirm; and CCC 31 sets these arguments apart from the natural sciences' sense of proof, which a fideist may use. No pinnable survey of ordinary believers is recorded.
